findings.text: Provides a stage-one invalidation service for nested guests that accepts a stage-two context plus address and encoded operation and reports success for recognized encodings and an invalid argument status otherwise.

Recognized encodings are normalized so full invalidations collapse to one inner shareable VM-all operation and each address based family collapses to its inner shareable address based counterpart, with shareability and related variants treated equivalently, followed by hypervisor synchronization and barrier before return.

VMID context is entered and exited only when a stage-two context is supplied, otherwise the operation runs in the current context, and the guest is assumed to have issued its store barrier before trapping.

Emulated handling is declined when the CPU runs with both extended hypervisor modes enabled and a pending virtualized TLB count is nonzero, allowing a slower path to serialize invalidation against walks, otherwise the trapping instruction is skipped and success is reported.

CPACR trap handling applies only without a newer nested feature, only in hypervisor context, and only for the CPACR encoding, mapping reads to the current CPTR value and writes through to CPTR followed by reactivation of related traps.

ZCR trap handling applies only for nested capable guests and the ZCR encoding when floating point state is not already guest owned, in which case floating point state is loaded and handling is always declined so the slow path completes the operation.
System register traps in VHE mode are offered in fixed order to invalidation, timer, CPACR, ZCR and finally generic handlers, with the first claimant deciding the outcome.

Implementation defined trap handling is inert without a specific PMU workaround capability, otherwise it synthesizes a 64-bit system register syndrome from an auxiliary fault register with length bit set and records it as the EL2 fault syndrome while always declining to claim the exit.

Exit dispatch table routes common classes for coprocessor, system register, vector, abort, watchpoint, return and memory operation exits to dedicated handlers and reserves a high code for the implementation defined workaround, with all other classes unhandled.
Hypervisor panic path never returns, deactivating traps when a virtual CPU is running and restoring host system state before reporting saved processor state, abort addresses and virtual CPU identity.
Two no-return entries capture current exception state or unexpected EL2 exceptions and forward to a common panic or unexpected exception routine.
Invalidation context carries a stage-two table pointer together with saved flags and copies of translation control and control registers.
Trace clock calibration uses a six hundred second maximum conversion window with one hundred millisecond initial delay and five hundred millisecond periodic update.
Trace clock object stores last counter and boot time epoch, conversion multiplier and shift with overflow guard, plus delayed work item and readiness completion.

Periodic clock worker snapshots boot time and counter, compares converted cycle progress against boot progress, warns when drift exceeds microsecond precision, recomputes conversion from measured rate, publishes new parameters to the hypervisor, and reschedules, with a fast forward of the epoch when nearing overflow even with no drift.
Enabling the trace clock captures a fresh snapshot, clears calibration, schedules the first update after the initial delay and waits for it, while disabling synchronously cancels pending work.
Host side trace buffer handle holds only a descriptor pointer and its allocated size.
Hypervisor mapping is skipped under protected mode and otherwise creates hypervisor mappings, while sharing operates one page at a time for metadata and data pages.

Backing storage size scales with requested trace size plus one page per possible CPU, is allocated as exact pages, mapped to the hypervisor, and recorded in the descriptor, with matching exact free on teardown.
Sharing walks per CPU ring descriptors sharing metadata then data pages and on failure unshares the partial CPU and all prior CPUs, while unsharing stops after a caller supplied CPU limit.

Trace buffer load rejects double load, checks descriptor size overflow and zero size, then proceeds through descriptor allocation, mapping, backing allocation, remote allocation, sharing and hypervisor load with reverse unwind on each failure, and unload validates identity before reversing those steps and clearing the handle.
Tracing enable first toggles the trace clock and then the hypervisor control, restoring the clock to its prior state if the hypervisor call fails.
Per CPU reader page swap and reset are thin forwards to hypervisor calls keyed by CPU number.
Event gating goes through the hypervisor under protected mode and otherwise temporarily maps the page holding the enable flag and updates it atomically before unmapping.
Trace clock status output always reports the boot clock source.

Trace control surface exposes a decimal write entry that forwards values to the hypervisor, filesystem entries for event injection and clock display, and a callback table binding initialization, buffer lifecycle, tracing toggle, reader management and event gating.
Hypervisor entry and exit reason codes map to a fixed small name table with out of range values clamped to the unknown entry.
Hypervisor trace header uses a standard include guard.
Standard and hypervisor feature bitmap widths are expressed as low bit masks derived from their respective bit count definitions.
Architecture SMC ranges span 32-bit calls from the version function to the top of the function field and 64-bit fast calls from function zero to the top of the function field.
Firmware register enumeration lists PSCI version, three architecture workarounds, and standard plus hypervisor and vendor bitmap registers in a fixed order.
Feature level encoding occupies the low four bits.
Fault address selection follows exception target level choosing EL2 or EL1 destination, and double fault behavior follows the effective EASE control bit.

Sixty four bit abort injection rewalks stage one tables on translation walk faults and abandons injection when the intermediate address is invalid or the walk cannot be resolved, otherwise reports an external abort, pends synchronous or asynchronous exception based on EASE, and records length, exception class and fault status with the fault address in the target level registers.
Thirty two bit fault encoding uses distinct external abort status values for LPAE and non LPAE modes together with single bit indicators for LPAE format and extended address enable.

Thirty two bit abort injection selects fault status from the translation control extended addressing bit, preserves the untouched half of the fault address register while inserting the new address, pends instruction or data abort and stores status in the appropriate syndrome register, with synchronous external aborts dispatched by EL1 bitness.

Synchronous external abort is directed to EL2 when trap controls request it or when running privileged with async masking plus a trap control, and exclusive atomic faults build a data abort syndrome with length set before delegating to nested synchronous injection.
Synchronous external abort injection is available to host code, forwarding to nested handling when in nested context with EL2 target and otherwise injecting locally with a positive completion status.
Synchronous external abort injection requires the virtual CPU mutex to be held by the caller.

Trace buffer load fails safely on size overflow, zero size, allocation failure or hypervisor rejection without leaking prior stages, and clock conversion guards against 64-bit overflow by widening multiplication when near the limit.
